key: Then she spoke, saying: ‘They were wont to speak in old time, saying: They shall surely ask counsel at Abel; and so they ended the matter.
s: From besieged Abel, where the rebel Sheba has fled, a wise woman calls to Joab; Rashi, on 20:18, reads her words as telling Joab he should first have offered peace, since had his men asked it, the town would at once have agreed.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok; ref 2 Samuel 20:18 and at [282,18] match; 26 words, one unit). Read Rashi, Radak and Metzudat David on 20:18 and 20:19 and Rashi across chapter 20 in the packet (no Midrash Rabbah on 2 Samuel). Rashi’s three lemmas on 20:18 say Joab should have spoken for peace first and not fought a town that answered peace, that had his troops asked Abel for peace, the townspeople would at once have made peace. The sentence’s reading carries those words without drift; Metzudat David (citing Deuteronomy 20:10) agrees, Radak (at 20:19) takes it as an old saying that a town is asked first whether it will make peace; no conflict to name. Plain sense fits 20:14 to 17 (Sheba, who raised his hand against the king, is besieged in Abel; a wise woman cries to Joab from the city). The siege is stated plainly. entry-check ok.
